newsitem.title: JAPAN: S.Africa's Manuel says rates may be cut in 1997.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Manuel says rates may be cut in 1997.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Wednesday the country's interest rates might be lowered later this year.
"Indications are positive for some reduction in interest rates later this year," Manuel, who is on a four-day visit to Japan, told a news conference.
His remarks followed the Tuesday release of South African producer price data for April, which came in lower than expected.
Last weekend in Switzerland, South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said it was quite possible that interest rates would decline later this year in light of the recent economic slowdown.
Asked about the country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth, Manuel said: "We still believe the country is on track for 2.5 percent growth this year."

The country's GDP showed a surprise fall of 1.0 percent in the first quarter from the previous quarter -- the first contraction since the first quarter of 1994 -- mainly due to a decline in agricultural production.
